name: Ho Chi Minh City
operatingHours: Metro Line 1 (Ben Thanh–Suoi Tien, the city's only line) runs ~5:00 AM–10:00 PM on weekdays and to ~11:00 PM on weekends and holidays, every ~5–8 min at peak and 10–15 min off-peak. Most of the city is covered by buses, Grab and taxis instead.
fareInfo: Line 1 single fares ~7,000–20,000 VND by distance (slightly less when paying cashless); a 1-day pass is ~40,000 VND and a 3-day pass ~90,000 VND. Gates take contactless bank cards, QR codes and e-wallets as well as tickets from station machines. City buses cost ~5,000–7,000 VND (airport bus 109 ~20,000 VND). Grab motorbike and car rides are cheap and widely used.

hotels.name: Rêve Ho Chi Minh City, Vignette Collection by IHG

sights.name: War Remnants Museum
sights.note: A sobering museum of the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective, with photojournalism, Agent Orange exhibits and US aircraft and tanks in the yard; some displays are graphic.

sights.name: Independence Palace
sights.note: The 1960s modernist presidential palace where a tank crashed the gates on 30 April 1975, kept as it was, with bunkers, war rooms and reception halls.

sights.name: Saigon Central Post Office
sights.note: A grand French-era post office from the 1890s with a vaulted iron-framed hall, old wall maps and working counters where you can still send postcards.

sights.name: Notre Dame Cathedral of Saigon
sights.note: Red-brick 19th-century cathedral with twin spires facing the post office; under long-running restoration, so the exterior is partly scaffolded and the interior is generally closed to visitors.
sights.hours: Under restoration (works due ~2027); view from outside

sights.name: Saigon Opera House
sights.note: A Belle Époque theatre from 1900 on Lam Son Square, best visited for an evening show such as the acrobatic bamboo-circus A O Show by Lune Production.
sights.hours: Exterior anytime; shows most evenings ~6:00 PM or 8:00 PM

sights.name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street & Ho Chi Minh Square
sights.note: A broad pedestrian boulevard running from the river to the colonial City Hall and its Ho Chi Minh statue; lively in the evenings with families, buskers and fountains.

sights.name: Ho Chi Minh City Book Street
sights.note: A shaded lane behind the post office lined with bookshop kiosks and cafés, a quiet break from the traffic.

sights.name: Bitexco Financial Tower (Saigon Skydeck)
sights.note: The lotus-bud skyscraper with a 49th-floor observation deck over the Saigon River and District 1; the helipad juts out from the 52nd floor.

sights.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
sights.note: Observation decks near the top of Vietnam's tallest building (461 m) in Binh Thanh, with sweeping city views best at sunset.

sights.name: Ben Thanh Market
sights.note: The city's best-known covered market under its clock tower, good for food stalls and souvenirs though prices are tourist-pitched; bargain hard.
sights.hours: ~6:00 AM–6:00 PM; street-food stalls around it into the evening

sights.name: Bui Vien Walking Street
sights.note: The backpacker strip's neon nightlife street, closed to traffic at night, packed with bars, plastic stools and street food; loud and boisterous.

sights.name: Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater
sights.note: Short performances of Vietnam's traditional water puppetry, with wooden figures gliding across a pool to live folk music.

sights.name: Tao Dan Park
sights.note: A big leafy park beside Independence Palace where locals exercise at dawn and songbird owners hang their cages in the café corner on mornings.

sights.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
sights.note: A smoky, atmospheric Taoist temple from 1909 packed with carved deities, and a turtle pond in the courtyard.

sights.name: Ba Thien Hau Temple
sights.note: A Cholon temple to the sea goddess Mazu built by Cantonese merchants, known for its ceramic roof figures and giant hanging incense coils.

sights.name: Museum of Vietnamese History
sights.note: A pagoda-style 1920s building at the zoo entrance covering Vietnam's past from prehistory to the Nguyen dynasty, including Champa sculpture.

sights.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
sights.note: A yellow colonial mansion with stained glass and an old lift, showing Vietnamese painting, lacquerwork and Champa art.

sights.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
sights.note: Far: about 60 km northwest, 1.5–2 h by road (or a boat from District 1). The preserved Viet Cong tunnel network at Ben Dinh, where visitors crawl through widened sections and see traps and hidden kitchens.

railStations.name: Saigon Railway Station
railStations.note: Terminus of the North–South Reunification Railway to Nha Trang, Da Nang, Hue and Hanoi (~30+ h), with sleeper berths; in District 3, not on the metro, about 15 min by Grab from District 1.
railStations.hours: Trains to individual timetables, ~6:00 AM–~10:00 PM departures.

airports.name: Tan Son Nhat International Airport
airports.transitNote: About 7 km north of District 1; not on the metro. Bus 109 runs from the terminals to Ben Thanh / Pham Ngu Lao in ~45 min (~20,000 VND), bus 152 is cheaper and slower; Grab or taxi ~25–40 min. Terminal 3 handles domestic flights. The new Long Thanh airport (LTH, ~40 km east) is due to start regular service from ~December 2026.
airports.hours: Bus 109: ~5:30 AM–~1:00 AM. Late arrivals: Grab or taxi.
